# First steps: local web pages 

---

## On your computer

- A web page begins with a file containing the page structure and content, e.g. ``index.html``

- open with VS Code: see the *source code* that was sent or downloaded

- open with a browser: see the *rendering* of the page with styles, links, images, AV content etc.

---

## On your Browser

- a *monster* software

- interprets commands in formal language

  - HTML: text + settings (invisible) + *mark up* tags
  
  - CSS: the style associated to tags

- let learn HTML by playing around on some web pages

- load pages by either clicking on the icon or press `alt` then the `File` menu


# Exercises

---

## Exercise A: learn by defacing

- open the *file system* of our computer (the yellow folders)
  
- navigate to `learn-web/15-lorem-boilerplate`

- right-click on `index.html` to open with VS Code

- on the upper right corner click on the window with magnifying lens

- scroll the code towards the center, try changing small parts to see how the preview changes

- exit without saving the changes

---

## Exercise B: study the basics

- Creativity is mediated by *strict rules* of HTML etc.

- apart from spaces, all characters and punctuation matter!


On [https://wdpg.io](https://wdpg.io) we did

- 1.1 and 1.2 to get started with HTML+CSS and rendering

- 2.1 to 2.8 to learn the basic mark-up tags, e.g., `p`, `b`, `em`... 


![](./wdpg-ch2.png)

---

## Exercise C: the Lorem exercise

- take the *boilerplate* project inside `learn-web/15-lorem-boilerplate`

- select file `rename-then-edit-me.html`, right-click then rename it. E.g., `ale-lorem.html` 

- select file `mystyle.css`, right-click then rename it. E.g., `ale-style.css` 

Alternatively, you can copy the two files and put them into any folder, e.g., `Downloads`, that sits outside  `learn-web `

---

Think of an intended reader of your page. E.g. 

- High-school students of Latin 

- teachers who are looking for classroom examples

- tourists of Rome/Latium who get curious about Latin lit 

- adult readers who enjoy Cicero's Latin prose

write HTML/CSS to create a suitable style

it should deploy all concepts learned in WDPG 2.1--2.8

Later, include concepts from WDPG 2.9 & 2.10
